sections.markdown:
**Original register inspected, 31 October 2026:** The original register copy of John Glasgow’s will is now inspected: Cumberland County Will Book C, printed pp.161–162, FamilySearch DGS 005534167, images 358–359. It is dated 14 March 1779 and the probate endorsement says 23 September 1779, correcting the earlier reported 3 September. It names wife Ann, daughter Lates, daughter Agnes and son Joseph; Ann is described as with child. The estate is to support wife and children for eight years before sale and distribution, with provision for the unborn child if it survives. Wife Ann and friend Thomas Cellar are appointed executors. James Neely, Joseph Glasgow and Mary Arter witness the will; the witness Joseph is distinct from the named son. This is an inspected register copy, not the separate original estate packet. The register supplies no married name or adult residence for Agnes, and therefore does not identify her as Nancy (Glascoe) Wright. Nancy’s father stays 37% Possible. The record-defined Lates and Joseph father links remain 98%; John’s own James-of-Moneymore father remains 30%. Ann’s maternity of the three already-born children is not expressly stated. No father or mother attachment, confidence percentage, identity merge or vital field is changed. Next test: estate distribution, guardianship or receipts after the eight-year provision, looking for Agnes/Nancy and a Wright husband; do not repeat the completed will-image inspection.

sections.title: Peters Township family assessment —20 October 2026
sections.markdown:
Fendrick’s checked 1944 abstract of the 1779 Peters Township will identifies John Glasgow’s wife Ann, daughters Lates and Agnes, and son Joseph. [Lates Glasgow (Glasgow-4028)](/people/glasgow-4028.html) and [Joseph Glasgow (Glasgow-4029)](/people/glasgow-4029.html) are the existing record-defined daughter and son accounts, not speculative later adult identifications. Assess John as their father at 98% each, strongly supported by the explicit abstracted relationship and matching will context. The manuscript has not been inspected, so this does not certify the spelling or completeness of the abstract. Joseph the son is distinct from the adult Joseph who witnessed the will.

Assess James of Moneymore, [James Glasgow II (Glasgow-1024)](/people/glasgow-1024.html), as John of Peters Township’s probable father at 76%. The 2024 Adams County family account specifically identifies the John who died in 1779 as brother of Robert, Arthur and Joseph. Fendrick’s abstract independently supplies a contemporary Joseph Glasgow witness in John’s Peters Township will; James Neely’s presence also fits the later Neely-associated emigrant family. Faris’s catalogue description identifies Robert’s father as James of Moneymore and reports four emigrant brothers. Together these identify a specific compatible family, rather than only another local James. Extend that probable father across the preferred fourth-brother identification, while rating John lower than the three established brothers because his place in that group depends partly on the later account and witness identification. Assess the John-to-each-established-brother relationship as probable at 83%.

potential_parentage.method: Automated leads use birth surnames—not married surnames—as parental eligibility, role-specific biological age limits, bounded and approximate-date uncertainty, household chronology, specific time-aware localities, mapped distance, tenancy succession, migration destinations and sex-aware Scottish naming positions across generations. People already attached as the subject's parents stay in the identity summary and are excluded from this alternative-candidate list, regardless of relationship confidence. The main calibration uses clues available on disconnected profiles; existing parent and sibling links are retained as comparison context rather than treated as transferable evidence. Common ordered names and grandparent-to-child echoes receive a small non-zero weight, so a John or James match can support several independent criteria without producing a lead alone. Rare names, repeated bearers and bundles across otherwise distinct branches receive substantially more weight according to catalogue frequency. An exact migration place is weighted by its rarity and repetition across both branches; a shared destination country is worth only one point. Extra weight is added only when at least three independent clue types converge: naming, locality, specific migration, household chronology or collateral networks. Sparse profiles retain a clearly labelled chronology-only fallback instead of disappearing. Countries, states, counties and research clusters do not count as a shared locality, and fallback, broad representative or kin-inferred coordinates are excluded from distance scoring. Shared descendant profiles are removed before branch-name comparison. A candidate already recorded as a parent-in-law is excluded. A confident or independently supported parent is treated as settled; uncertain and unassessed attachments remain open to alternative comparison. A different linked parent, an uncle/aunt or grandparent path, and a matching existing child profile prevent an alternative from being classified as a strong direct-parent lead until the underlying tree conflict or duplicate is resolved. Familiar forms such as Bessie are normalised. Surname remains an eligibility filter worth zero points.
potential_parentage.warning: Naming customs, shared farms and occupations are circumstantial. Children, spouses and collateral relatives may be missing, and tree-derived family networks are not independent evidence. Scores rank research leads; they do not prove parentage.

wikitree_update.remote_wikitext:
== Biography ==
Thomas and Nancy emigrated from Somerset County, Maryland to Vevay, Indiana in 1811. They had 9 children. Thomas had 5 siblings.


== Research Notes ==

=== Possible identity as Agnes Glasgow ===

John Glasgow of Peters Township made his will on 14 March 1779. A published abstract names a daughter Agnes, as well as his wife [[Unknown-764130|Ann]], daughter [[Glasgow-4028|Lates or possibly Lettice]], son [[Glasgow-4029|Joseph]], and an unborn child.<ref name="JohnWill">Cumberland County, Pennsylvania, Will Book C, p. 161, will of John Glasgow, dated 14 March 1779 and proved 3 September 1779. The volume is identified as Will Book C, 1777-1779, Pennsylvania State Archives roll 1494, in the [https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/phmc/documents/archives/research-online/documents/Cumberland.pdf Cumberland County records guide]. The entry is also listed in the [https://www.sampubco.com/wills/pa/pacumberland01.htm published will-book index].</ref>

This profile is a plausible candidate for Agnes because Nancy was born about 1778, her surname was recorded as Glascoe, and her existing profile previously had no identified parents. Nancy later lived in Somerset County, Maryland, which is compatible with but does not prove a connection to the Peters Township family.

“Nancy” can occur as a familiar form related to Ann or Agnes, but name usage alone is not identity evidence. No probate, guardianship, marriage or land record presently identifies Nancy as John Glasgow's daughter. Both parent relationships are therefore marked uncertain.


=== Wright intermarriage network ===

Nancy married [[Wright-42790|Thomas Wright]]. Four additional marriages to Wrights occur in the immediate family or documented descendants of [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]], the proposed brother of [[Glasgow-4027|John Glasgow]]:

* Robert married [[Wright-52925|Peggy Wright]].
* Robert's grandson [[Glasgow-9|Samuel Steele Glasgow]] married [[Wright-50850|Martha Carol Wright]].
* Robert's grandson [[Glasgow-1938|William Madison Glasgow]] married [[Wright-55176|Margaret Ann Wright]].
* William Madison's sister [[Glasgow-1926|Mary Ann Glasgow]] married [[Wright-12727|Robert Lowers Wright]].

William Madison and Mary Ann were children of [[Glasgow-563|William Glasgow]], Robert's son. Margaret Ann Wright and Robert Lowers Wright were both born at Newburgh, Orange County, New York, suggesting that those two later spouses may have belonged to the same Wright family, although their parents are not identified on their profiles. Martha was born in Adams County, Ohio, while Peggy's parents and birthplace remain unknown.

Repeated Glasgow-Wright marriages are consistent with a wider family and associate network and add circumstantial support to the proposal that Nancy was the Agnes named in John Glasgow's 1779 will. == Biography ==
=== Original register review — 31 October 2026 ===
The original register copy of John Glasgow’s will is now inspected: Cumberland County Will Book C, printed pp.161–162, FamilySearch DGS 005534167, images 358–359. It is dated 14 March 1779 and the probate endorsement says 23 September 1779, correcting the earlier reported 3 September. It names wife Ann, daughter Lates, daughter Agnes and son Joseph; Ann is described as with child. The estate is to support wife and children for eight years before sale and distribution, with provision for the unborn child if it survives. Wife Ann and friend Thomas Cellar are appointed executors. James Neely, Joseph Glasgow and Mary Arter witness the will; the witness Joseph is distinct from the named son. This is an inspected register copy, not the separate original estate packet.

The register supplies no married name or adult residence for Agnes, and therefore does not identify her as Nancy (Glascoe) Wright. Nancy’s father stays 37% Possible. The record-defined Lates and Joseph father links remain 98%; John’s own James-of-Moneymore father remains 30%. Ann’s maternity of the three already-born children is not expressly stated. No father or mother attachment, confidence percentage, identity merge or vital field is changed. Next test: estate distribution, guardianship or receipts after the eight-year provision, looking for Agnes/Nancy and a Wright husband; do not repeat the completed will-image inspection.<ref>Cumberland County, Pennsylvania, Will Book C, pp.161–162, John Glasgow, will dated 14 March 1779, proved 23 September 1779; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899B-J7VD opening] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899B-J761 continuation/probate], DGS005534167 images358–359, inspected 31 October 2026.</ref>

Thomas and Nancy emigrated from Somerset County, Maryland to Vevay, Indiana in 1811. They had 9 children. Thomas had 5 siblings.


== Research Notes ==
=== Peters Township family review,20 October 2026 ===

John of Peters Township remains a possible father at 37%, conditional on identifying Nancy with the will’s daughter Agnes. No Maryland-to-Pennsylvania identity bridge is established.

Fendrick’s checked 1944 abstract of the 1779 Peters Township will identifies John Glasgow’s wife Ann, daughters Lates and Agnes, and son Joseph. [[Glasgow-4028|Lates Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-4029|Joseph Glasgow]] are the existing record-defined daughter and son accounts, not speculative later adult identifications. Assess John as their father at 98% each, strongly supported by the explicit abstracted relationship and matching will context. The manuscript has not been inspected, so this does not certify the spelling or completeness of the abstract. Joseph the son is distinct from the adult Joseph who witnessed the will.

Assess James of Moneymore, [[Glasgow-1024|James Glasgow II]], as John of Peters Township’s probable father at 76%. The 2024 Adams County family account specifically identifies the John who died in 1779 as brother of Robert, Arthur and Joseph. Fendrick’s abstract independently supplies a contemporary Joseph Glasgow witness in John’s Peters Township will; James Neely’s presence also fits the later Neely-associated emigrant family. Faris’s catalogue description identifies Robert’s father as James of Moneymore and reports four emigrant brothers. Together these identify a specific compatible family, rather than only another local James. Extend that probable father across the preferred fourth-brother identification, while rating John lower than the three established brothers because his place in that group depends partly on the later account and witness identification. Assess the John-to-each-established-brother relationship as probable at 83%.

The original will and probate packet remain uninspected. The checked abstract gives 1779, not the execution/probate days; existing 14 March and 3 September date limits are preserved from the earlier cited profile account, not newly verified. The will index verifies John’s locator, Cumberland Will Book C, p.161, but supplies no relatives. Ann is named as wife, not expressly mother of the children; her existing maternal attachments remain unassessed. Nancy (Glascoe) Wright is only a possible identification of Agnes: an approximately 1778 birth fits a child alive in 1779 and Agnes/Nancy can be compatible name forms, but the later Maryland/Indiana household has no inspected parent, guardianship or estate bridge to Peters Township. Her existing John father is therefore possible at 37%, not confident. The witness Joseph is not proved to be Joseph of Wythe County. The family-history article may depend on Faris and is not independent corroboration of his genealogy. The 1944 abstract, not the original will, was inspected.</ref>


=== Possible identity as Agnes Glasgow ===

John Glasgow of Peters Township made his will on 14 March 1779. A published abstract names a daughter Agnes, as well as his wife [[Unknown-764130|Ann]], daughter [[Glasgow-4028|Lates or possibly Lettice]], son [[Glasgow-4029|Joseph]], and an unborn child.<ref name="JohnWill">Cumberland County, Pennsylvania, Will Book C, p. 161, will of John Glasgow, dated 14 March 1779 and proved 3 September 1779. The volume is identified as Will Book C, 1777-1779, Pennsylvania State Archives roll 1494, in the [https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/phmc/documents/archives/research-online/documents/Cumberland.pdf Cumberland County records guide]. The entry is also listed in the [https://www.sampubco.com/wills/pa/pacumberland01.htm published will-book index].</ref>

This profile is a plausible candidate for Agnes because Nancy was born about 1778, her surname was recorded as Glascoe, and her existing profile previously had no identified parents. Nancy later lived in Somerset County, Maryland, which is compatible with but does not prove a connection to the Peters Township family.

“Nancy” can occur as a familiar form related to Ann or Agnes, but name usage alone is not identity evidence. No probate, guardianship, marriage or land record presently identifies Nancy as John Glasgow's daughter. Both parent relationships are therefore marked uncertain.


=== Wright intermarriage network ===

Nancy married [[Wright-42790|Thomas Wright]]. Four additional marriages to Wrights occur in the immediate family or documented descendants of [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]], the proposed brother of [[Glasgow-4027|John Glasgow]]:

* Robert married [[Wright-52925|Peggy Wright]].
* Robert's grandson [[Glasgow-9|Samuel Steele Glasgow]] married [[Wright-50850|Martha Carol Wright]].
* Robert's grandson [[Glasgow-1938|William Madison Glasgow]] married [[Wright-55176|Margaret Ann Wright]].
* William Madison's sister [[Glasgow-1926|Mary Ann Glasgow]] married [[Wright-12727|Robert Lowers Wright]].

William Madison and Mary Ann were children of [[Glasgow-563|William Glasgow]], Robert's son. Margaret Ann Wright and Robert Lowers Wright were both born at Newburgh, Orange County, New York, suggesting that those two later spouses may have belonged to the same Wright family, although their parents are not identified on their profiles. Martha was born in Adams County, Ohio, while Peggy's parents and birthplace remain unknown.

Repeated Glasgow-Wright marriages are consistent with a wider family and associate network and add circumstantial support to the proposal that Nancy was the Agnes named in John Glasgow's 1779 will. No source yet connects Thomas Wright to Peggy, Martha, Margaret or Robert Wright, so this pattern does not prove Nancy's parentage or establish kinship between the Wright spouses.
